differential responding as a function for auditory stimulus intensity without different reinforcement is not possible.
differential responding as a function (or function of the function) of stimulus intensity is possible without differential reinforcement.

the acquisition and extinction of a response maintained by the presentation of a stimulus.

the acquisition of differential control by auditory stimuli is a function of the stimulus intensity dynamism of those stimuli and that the necessary conditions for stimulus control are the same whether the stimuli are visual or auditory.

stimulus intensity dynamism may be more likely to be established when the number of auditory stimuli is low and the intensity of the stimulus is high.
